name: pynvvideocodec
raw_meta_yaml:
context:
  version: "2.2.3"
  cuda_build_string: cuda${{ cuda_compiler_version | version_to_buildstring }}

package:
  name: pynvvideocodec
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://api.ngc.nvidia.com/v2/resources/nvidia/pynvvideocodec/versions/v${{ version }}/files/PyNvVideoCodec_${{ version }}.zip
  sha256: 29f7c0694d683266c563aca9a4f8e979ba0c5dce8f0ccc1efe500073e0948be0
  patches:
    - 0001-use-conda-dependencies.patch
    - 0002-delay-load-windows-cuda-driver.patch

build:
  number: 2
  string: ${{ cuda_build_string }}_py${{ python | version_to_buildstring }}h${{ hash }}_${{ build_number }}
  skip:
    - cuda_compiler_version == "None"
    - not (linux or win)
    - ppc64le

requirements:
  build:
    - ${{ compiler('c') }}
    - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
    - ${{ compiler('cuda') }}
    - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
    - cmake >=3.21
    - ninja
  host:
    - python
    - pip
    - setuptools >=42
    - wheel
    - packaging
    - scikit-build
    - numpy
    - pybind11 >=2.12
    - dlpack >=0.8
    - cuda-version ${{ cuda_compiler_version }}.*
    - cuda-cudart-dev
    - if: not win
      then: cuda-driver-dev
    - ffmpeg
  run:
    - python
    - __cuda >=12.2
    - ${{ pin_compatible("cuda-version", lower_bound="x", upper_bound="x") }}
    - cuda-cudart
  ignore_run_exports:
    by_name:
      - cuda-version
    from_package:
      - cuda-cudart-dev
      - if: not win
        then: cuda-driver-dev

# Importing PyNvVideoCodec queries the NVIDIA driver. Load the extensions
# directly instead, so CI can check them without a GPU or driver.
tests:
  - script:
      - python -m pip check
      - python test_extensions.py
    requirements:
      run:
        - pip
        - if: not win
          then: cuda-driver-dev
    files:
      recipe:
        - test_extensions.py

about:
  homepage: https://pypi.org/project/pynvvideocodec/
  summary: NVIDIA Python library for hardware-accelerated video encoding and decoding
  description: |
    PyNvVideoCodec is NVIDIA's Python-based library that provides simple yet powerful Python APIs for hardware-accelerated video encoding and decoding on NVIDIA GPUs.

    PyNvVideoCodec is built on top of the Video Codec SDK and offers encode, decode, and transcode performance on par with it.
  license: MIT
  license_file:
    - LICENSE.txt
    - NOTICES.txt
  documentation: https://docs.nvidia.com/video-technologies/pynvvideocodec/index.html
  repository: https://catalog.ngc.nvidia.com/orgs/nvidia/resources/pynvvideocodec

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - shermansiu
    - conda-forge/cuda
